Brickwall Filter.Slope: Steepness of the cut past the cutoff, in dB per octave
Brickwall Filter.SoftBypass: Lets the signal through unprocessed, fading in and out without clicks

Comb Filter.Mode: Adds (Plus) or subtracts (Minus) the delayed signal, moving where the comb peaks fall
Comb Filter.Algorithm: Classic or Modern comb sound; Modern adds interpolation, smoothing and saturation
Comb Filter.Q: Emphasis at the cutoff; high settings make it ring or self-oscillate
Comb Filter.KeyTracking: Key tracking relative to C3; at 100%, C4 raises the frequency one octave

Compressor Expander.AutoMakeUp: Adds automatic compensation for gain reduction, on top of make-up gain
Compressor Expander.MakeUpGain: Gain applied after compression to compensate for gain reduction
Compressor Expander.CompThreshold: Level above which the compressor starts reducing gain
Compressor Expander.CompRatio: Sets how strongly the level above the threshold is reduced
Compressor Expander.CompAttack: Time to reach full gain reduction once the threshold is crossed
Compressor Expander.CompRelease: Time to return to unity once the level falls below the threshold
Compressor Expander.GateThreshold: Level below which the expander starts attenuating the signal
Compressor Expander.GateRatio: Below gate threshold: above 1 expands, below 1 lifts low levels, 1 is neutral
Compressor Expander.GateAttack: Time for the gate to open once the level rises above its threshold
Compressor Expander.GateRelease: Time for the gate to close once the level falls below its threshold
Compressor Expander.Mix: Balance between the dry and processed signal

Convolver.Dry: Level of the unprocessed signal in the output
Convolver.Wet: Level of the convolved signal in the output
Convolver.NormalizePower: Normalizes the impulse response power to keep output level consistent

Crossover Filter.LowFrequency: Lower crossover frequency, used by the low pass and band pass types
Crossover Filter.HighFrequency: Upper crossover frequency, used by the high pass and band pass types

Diffuse Delay.TimeSpread: Time spread of the diffusion in % of delay time
Diffuse Delay.Diffusion: Controls the amount of diffusion in %
Diffuse Delay.Feedback: Controls the amount of feedback in %
Diffuse Delay.Damp: Controls the amount of damping in %
Diffuse Delay.CrossTalk: Amount of feedback cross-talk between channels in %
Diffuse Delay.Mix: Controls the mixing between dry and wet signals
Diffuse Delay.Randomness: Controls the amount of delay randomisation in %

Digital Filter.Slope: Steepness of the filter slope in dB per octave
Digital Filter.Freq: Cutoff or center frequency of the filter
Digital Filter.KeyTracking: How much the frequency follows the played note; negative tracks downward
Digital Filter.Spread: Offsets the filter frequency between channels to widen the stereo image
Digital Filter.Q: Emphasis around the filter frequency, without effect on the 6 dB slope
Digital Filter.Gain: Boost or cut applied by the low shelf, high shelf and peak shapes
Digital Filter.Bandwidth: Width in octaves of the band pass, notch and peak shapes

Digital Eq.StereoMode: Assigns bands to left/right or mid/side channels
Digital Eq.Transpose: Shifts the frequency of every band, in octaves
Digital Eq.KeyTracking: Amount by which band frequencies follow the played note
Digital Eq.OverallGain: Output level applied after the bands
Digital Eq.GainScale: Scales band gains and output level, inverting below zero
Digital Eq.Enabled1: Turns this band on or off
Digital Eq.Type1: Shape: low pass, high pass, band pass, notch, low shelf, high shelf or peak
Digital Eq.Slope1: Steepness of this band, in dB per octave
Digital Eq.Channels1: Restricts this band to a single channel or applies it to all of them
Digital Eq.Freq1: Cutoff or center frequency of this band
Digital Eq.Q1: Resonance of this band around its frequency
Digital Eq.Gain1: Boost or cut applied by this band
Digital Eq.Bandwidth1: Frequency width of this band, in octaves

Diode Clipper.Drive: Sets how hard the signal is pushed into the diode pair
Diode Clipper.Tone: Lowpass cutoff inside the clipping circuit
Diode Clipper.HighPass: Highpass cutoff inside the clipping circuit
Diode Clipper.Asymmetry: Unbalances the diodes, shifting even-to-odd harmonic ratio

Dispersor.Spread: How far transients are smeared in time by dispersion
Dispersor.Freq: Frequency the dispersion curve is centred on
Dispersor.Order: First order for gentler smear, second order for sharper
Dispersor.Stages: Number of chained dispersion stages; more gives denser smear

Drive.DriveAmount: How far the signal is driven into the selected curve
Drive.Mode: Distortion curve: Analog soft rounding, Mild cubic bend, Strong hard clipping
Drive.Oversampling: Internal oversampling factor, trading CPU for reduced aliasing

Dual Delay X.TapeDrive: Amount of overdrive applied to the delay input
Dual Delay X.Reflection: Toggles rotation or reflection of stereo feedback
Dual Delay X.DelayTime: Main delay time between echoes; beat ratio when synced
Dual Delay X.LowCut: Lowcut/highpass cutoff in the feedback path
Dual Delay X.HighCut: Highcut/lowpass cutoff in the feedback path
Dual Delay X.PeakFreq: Center frequency of peaking EQ in the feedback path
Dual Delay X.PeakGain: Gain in decibels of peaking EQ in the feedback path
Dual Delay X.PeakQ: Q or width of peaking EQ in the feedback path
Dual Delay X.PeakCompensation: Gain reduction on peaking EQ to avoid feedback instability
Dual Delay X.Feedback: Amount of delay fed back to the input
Dual Delay X.Mix: Ratio between dry and wet signal paths
Dual Delay X.Rotation: Rotation or reflection angle applied to feedback stereo field
Dual Delay X.InputWidth: Input stereo width before the delay; 0% is mono
Dual Delay X.OutputWidth: Width of the stereo image after the delay
Dual Delay X.DelayRatio: Ratio of left to right delay times; 0.66 dotted, 0.5 half, 0.33 triplet
Dual Delay X.FeedbackRatio: Ratio between left and right feedback amounts
Dual Delay X.InputRotation: Rotates stereo input; +45 is LR to MS, -45 the reverse
Dual Delay X.OutputRotation: Rotates stereo output; -45 is MS to LR, +45 the reverse
Dual Delay X.ModDepth: Amount of modulation applied to delay time, in cents
Dual Delay X.ModRate: Rate of modulation applied to delay time
Dual Delay X.ModChannelOffset: Difference in modulation between left and right delays
Dual Delay X.Interpolation: Delay read quality: Drop, Linear, Cubic
Dual Delay X.DispersionFreq: Center frequency where dispersion delay is maximal
Dual Delay X.DiffusionAmount: Level of diffusive delays relative to the main delay
Dual Delay X.CrusherFreq: Sampling frequency of the virtual digital converter
Dual Delay X.CrusherBits: Bit depth of the virtual digital converter
Dual Delay X.Filtering: Enables the filtering section in the feedback loop
Dual Delay X.DuckerThreshold: Audio input threshold for the ducker

Ensemble 505.Mode: Ensemble style, from most subtle to most pronounced
Ensemble 505.Tone: Lowpass cutoff applied along the ensemble path
Ensemble 505.Mix: Balance between input signal and ensemble output

Exciter.InputGain: Boosts or cuts the signal feeding the excitation stage
Exciter.Amount: How hard the signal is driven into the excitation stage
Exciter.Mix: Amount of excited signal blended into the output
Exciter.Mode: Tape sine saturation or Tube level-tracking harmonics
Exciter.Oversampling: Internal oversampling factor, trading CPU for reduced aliasing

FET Compressor.Ratio: 4:1 to 20:1, plus All (all four ratio buttons jammed together)
FET Compressor.Attack: Panel dial 1 (slowest) to 7 (fastest), about 5.6 ms to 0.1 ms
FET Compressor.InputGain: Gain into signal and detector, -20 to 20 dB
FET Compressor.OutputGain: Makeup gain at the output, -40 to 40 dB
FET Compressor.Drive: Output line amp drive, -6 to 40 dB, level-compensated
FET Compressor.Mix: Blend between dry input and compressed signal

Feedback Compressor.Threshold: Output level above which the feedback detector reduces gain
Feedback Compressor.Ratio: Compression ratio above threshold, scaling effective attack time
Feedback Compressor.Knee: Width of the soft knee around the threshold
Feedback Compressor.DynamicRange: Caps the maximum gain reduction applied
Feedback Compressor.Attack: Time for gain reduction to build up, stretched by ratio
Feedback Compressor.Release: Time the detector takes to release gain reduction
Feedback Compressor.Makeup: Amount of automatic gain compensation applied
Feedback Compressor.Mix: Balance between dry and compressed signal for parallel compression
Feedback Compressor.OutputGain: Gain at the very output, after compression and mix
Feedback Compressor.InputGain: Gain applied before the signal reaches the compressor

Feedback Machine.DelayTime: Time chain output is delayed before reinjection at input
Feedback Machine.Feedback: Amount of chain output reinjected at the input
Feedback Machine.Mix: Balance between dry input and chain output

Feedforward Compressor.UpwardMode: Enables or disables compression of levels above upward threshold
Feedforward Compressor.UpwardThreshold: Detected level above which the upward segment starts acting
Feedforward Compressor.UpwardRatio: Input-to-output ratio above the upward threshold
Feedforward Compressor.UpwardKnee: Width of the smooth transition around the upward threshold
Feedforward Compressor.DownwardMode: Below threshold: nothing, compression lifting quiet levels, or expansion
Feedforward Compressor.DownwardThreshold: Detected level below which the downward segment starts acting
Feedforward Compressor.DownwardRatio: Input-to-output ratio below the downward threshold
Feedforward Compressor.DownwardKnee: Width of the smooth transition around the downward threshold
Feedforward Compressor.Attack: Time the detector takes to follow a rise in level
Feedforward Compressor.Release: Time the detector takes to follow a fall in level
Feedforward Compressor.DetectionMode: Level measured as peak or as RMS average
Feedforward Compressor.AutoMakeup: Automatic gain compensation bringing loudest output to 0 dB
Feedforward Compressor.Mix: Blend between untouched input and processed signal
